doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Growling, high notes and fingerings
summary: Altissimo via regular fingerings, voice in the horn, Glazunov joke.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Do you ever growl into your horn.
Sometimes, yeah. A lot of times when I’m way up in the high register I’ll like to put my voice into it. It seems to just naturally happen too.
Like you’re just playing so hard and all of a sudden you’re like ahhhh — into the horn.
As a matter of fact, going back to that clip I was watching you on that tune, at one point you were popping out these [scats] I mean like way high.
I mean do you have — people say well how do you play high like that? Are you doing overtones or do you just have special fingerings that you know sort of work.

Fingerings, like high G — that’s not going to work right now [scale] sorry, you may want to edit this part. [more horn] Yeah, all the regular fingerings usually is what I do. And then I’ll do kind of I guess random stuff where it’s kind of [scats] like in between notes and stuff. But not as much as like the overtone thing like you were talking about, it’s mostly fingerings.
Right, that was more of a classical thing to learn, of the Sigurd Rascher.
Right. I haven’t seen the stuff but I know it.
Well some day I’m going to hear a clip of you playing with Soulive or your own band or whatever and I’m expecting to hear a quote from the Glazunov Concerto. Yes. Okay. So see if you can that in.
Yes. Okay. I will, I will. Yeah, but that would be funny.
